after.description: The rabbitfish is a chimaera with a cartilage skeleton, a long tapering tail, and permanent tooth plates for crushing shellfish.

edits.before: Often referred to as a "ghost shark," this bizarre creature is famous for its shimmering, scaleless skin, large rabbit-like eyes.
edits.after: The rabbitfish is a chimaera with a cartilage skeleton, a long tapering tail, and permanent tooth plates for crushing shellfish.

after.description: Six pairs of frilly gill slits give this deep-water shark its name. Its eel-like body and rows of three-pointed teeth help it capture prey.
A swift, pelagic shark that gets its name from its exceptionally smooth, soft skin, which is covered in densely packed overlapping scales.
Nurse sharks can rest completely still on the ocean floor and pump water directly over their gills to breathe, unlike many other shark species.
Long-spined sea urchins graze on algae and help keep reef surfaces clear. Their slender spines defend them while tube feet grip and move over rocks.
The magnificent anemone anchors to reef rock with a sticky foot. Its stinging tentacles catch prey and shelter several species of anemonefish.

edits.before: Sea anemones anchor to rock and hunt with stinging tentacles packed with tiny harpoons. Some host clownfish, trading shelter for scraps.
edits.after: The magnificent anemone anchors to reef rock with a sticky foot. Its stinging tentacles catch prey and shelter several species of anemonefish.

after.description: Arrow crabs tiptoe on stilt-like legs, their long “arrow” snout probing crevices. At night they scavenge around for leftovers.
Peacock mantis shrimp smash hard-shelled prey with club-like limbs. Their rapid strikes create cavitation bubbles that collapse in a second impact.

edits.before: Mantis shrimp hunt with specialized clubs or spears. Club-bearing species strike so fast that collapsing cavitation bubbles add a second impact.
edits.after: Peacock mantis shrimp smash hard-shelled prey with club-like limbs. Their rapid strikes create cavitation bubbles that collapse in a second impact.

after.description: Leather stars have smooth, rubbery skin and a garlic-like odor. Tube feet carry them over rocky Pacific shores as they feed on anemones and other prey.
Scarlet cleaner shrimp wave long white antennae at cleaning stations. Fish visit to have parasites and dead tissue removed from their skin and mouths.
Giant tritons are large predatory sea snails that hunt crown-of-thorns starfish, subduing them with a paralyzing bite.
Greater blue-ringed octopuses flash vivid blue rings when threatened. These small reef hunters use potent venom to subdue crabs and other prey.

edits.before: Octopuses change color and texture in a blink, melting into reef or rock. With eight clever arms and hundreds of suckers, they solve puzzles—then vanish in a puff of ink.
edits.after: Greater blue-ringed octopuses flash vivid blue rings when threatened. These small reef hunters use potent venom to subdue crabs and other prey.

after.description: Eastern oysters filter plankton from coastal water. Their rough shells grow together into reefs that shelter fish, crabs, and other small animals.

edits.before: Oysters are a vital component of marine ecosystems, primarily functioning as filter feeders that significantly improve water quality and create complex reef habitats.
edits.after: Eastern oysters filter plankton from coastal water. Their rough shells grow together into reefs that shelter fish, crabs, and other small animals.

after.description: The swimming sea cucumber feeds on seafloor sediment, then swims with a webbed veil. Its transparent body reveals the coiled gut inside.

edits.before: Deep-sea sea cucumbers feed on organic particles on or near the seafloor. Their soft bodies and feeding tentacles come in many shapes across species.
edits.after: The swimming sea cucumber feeds on seafloor sediment, then swims with a webbed veil. Its transparent body reveals the coiled gut inside.

after.description: Common brittle stars raise their spiny arms to catch food particles from passing water. A lost arm can regrow after a narrow escape.

edits.before: Brittle stars move with slender, flexible arms joined to a central disc. Many can shed an arm to escape a predator and later regrow it.
edits.after: Common brittle stars raise their spiny arms to catch food particles from passing water. A lost arm can regrow after a narrow escape.

after.description: When threatened, it doesn't ink; instead, it cloaks itself by pulling its webbed arms over its head and releases glowing, bioluminescent clouds.
Giant isopods are deep-sea relatives of woodlice. Their armored bodies protect them as they scavenge, and a slow metabolism helps them endure long fasts.
Giant tube worms live at hydrothermal vents. Without a mouth or gut, adults rely on internal bacteria that use chemicals from vent fluids to make food.
Boreal glass squid have transparent bodies and large eyes. Light organs beneath the eyes help conceal their silhouettes in the dim ocean.

edits.before: Peacock squid have large eyes and nearly transparent bodies. Light organs beneath the eyes help hide their silhouettes from predators below.
edits.after: Boreal glass squid have transparent bodies and large eyes. Light organs beneath the eyes help conceal their silhouettes in the dim ocean.

after.description: A Portuguese man o' war is a colony of specialized zooids. Its gas-filled float rides at the surface while long, stinging tentacles capture prey below.
Market squid live only about six to nine months. They gather to mate and lay egg capsules on the seafloor, then die after spawning.
The Australian box jellyfish has a cube-shaped bell and clusters of eyes. Its long tentacles carry powerful venom for catching fish and shrimp.
Singapore parrotfish graze reef surfaces with fused, beak-like teeth. Terminal-phase fish have a distinctive green throat and brightly edged scales.

edits.before: Parrotfish scrape food from reef surfaces with beak-like teeth, helping produce sand. Some species sleep inside protective mucus cocoons.
edits.after: Singapore parrotfish graze reef surfaces with fused, beak-like teeth. Terminal-phase fish have a distinctive green throat and brightly edged scales.

after.description: Protected by a rigid, box-like body, longhorn cowfish graze on small bottom-dwelling prey. When severely stressed, they can release toxic mucus.
Giant frogfish blend into sponges and reef growth, then lure prey with a modified fin spine. An expanding mouth pulls the victim in with a sudden gulp.

edits.before: Frogfish hide among reef growth and lure prey with a modified dorsal-fin spine. Their expanding mouths suck in unsuspecting animals in a rapid gulp.
edits.after: Giant frogfish blend into sponges and reef growth, then lure prey with a modified fin spine. An expanding mouth pulls the victim in with a sudden gulp.

after.description: Often called a "rattail" because of its slender, whip-like tail, this deep-sea fish can live for over 70 years in extreme pressures.
Female humpback anglerfish carry a lure lit by symbiotic bacteria. It dangles above the mouth, drawing prey close in the darkness of the deep sea.
Fangtooth fish have enormous teeth for their small bodies. Special sockets in the roof of the mouth make room for the long lower fangs.
The black swallower has an elastic stomach that can hold prey larger than itself. This adaptation helps it take advantage of scarce deep-sea meals.
Tripod fish stand above the seabed on three elongated fin rays. Facing into the current, they spread their pectoral fins to help detect drifting prey.
Ballyhoo halfbeaks swim near the surface with a long lower jaw and a short upper jaw. They feed on drifting plants and small animals.

edits.before: Halfbeaks have a long lower jaw and a much shorter upper jaw. These surface-dwelling fish may leap or skip across the water to escape predators.
edits.after: Ballyhoo halfbeaks swim near the surface with a long lower jaw and a short upper jaw. They feed on drifting plants and small animals.

after.description: Hound needlefish hunt near the surface with long jaws lined with sharp teeth. They chase small fish and may leap clear of the water.

edits.before: Needlefish hunt near the surface with long jaws lined with sharp teeth. When startled, they can leap clear of the water.
edits.after: Hound needlefish hunt near the surface with long jaws lined with sharp teeth. They chase small fish and may leap clear of the water.
